root_cause.text: The ivpu metric-stream `get_info_ioctl` path failed to validate that the firmware-reported `info_size` fit within the allocated buffer object, so an oversized size could lead to an incorrect buffer copy and overflow in `drivers/accel/ivpu/ivpu_ms.c`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (info_size > ivpu_bo_size(bo)) { ... ret = -EOVERFLOW; goto unlock; }` before the existing `args->buffer_size < info_size` check, and the commit message says it fixes “buffer overflow check in MS get_info_ioctl” by rejecting cases where “the firmware returns a size larger than the buffer.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (info_size > ivpu_bo_size(bo)) { ... ret = -EOVERFLOW; goto unlock; }` before the existing `args->buffer_size < info_size` check, and the commit message says it fixes “buffer overflow check in MS get_info_ioctl” by rejecting cases where “the firmware returns a size larger than the buffer.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an overflow check in `ivpu_ms_get_info_ioctl` to reject MS info sizes larger than the backing buffer.
intent_record.what: A new size check was added after the existing info retrieval: if `info_size` is greater than `ivpu_bo_size(bo)`, the code logs a ratelimited warning, sets `ret` to `-EOVERFLOW`, and jumps to `unlock` before the later `args->buffer_size < info_size` check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the ioctl now rejects cases where the reported MS info would exceed the allocated buffer object size, preventing an overflow/overread condition and returning an explicit overflow error instead of continuing with an invalid size.

grouping_result.intent: Add an overflow check in `ivpu_ms_get_info_ioctl` to reject MS info sizes larger than the backing buffer.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the reported root cause by adding validation in ivpu_ms_get_info_ioctl to ensure the firmware-reported info_size does not exceed the allocated buffer, preventing the overflow.

candidates.rationale: This is the pre-fix control flow entering the copy path without any check that the firmware-reported info_size fits the allocated buffer. The missing size validation is what allowed an oversized copy to proceed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This pre-fix control-flow check allows execution to continue into the information-copy path without validating that the firmware-reported info_size fits within the allocated buffer, which is the missing size validation underlying the overflow.

Author: Tomasz Rusinowicz <tomasz.rusinowicz@intel.com>

    accel/ivpu: Add NPU profiling support
    
    Implement time based Metric Streamer profiling UAPI.
    
    This is a generic mechanism allowing user mode tools to sample
    NPU metrics. These metrics are defined by the FW and transparent to
    the driver.
    
    The user space can check for this feature by checking
    DRM_IVPU_CAP_METRIC_STREA
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is an unchecked firmware-reported `info_size` that can exceed the allocated buffer before copying to userspace. In this snippet, `ivpu_ms_get_info_ioctl()` explicitly validates the size: `ret = ivpu_jsm_metric_streamer_info(..., &info_size);` followed by `if (args->buffer_size < info_size) { ret = -ENOSPC; goto unlock; }` before `copy_to_user(..., ivpu_bo_vaddr(bo), info_size)`. This means the code already contains the needed bounds check against the user-provided buffer size, so the overflow-prone construct is not present here and the fix is already present.
